blurb: Some standard-library enums, among them `FetchError` and `Method`, are extensible: a minor release may add a variant. So is the built-in `HttpResult`, whose RFC 9110 status vocabulary grows in 1.x minor releases. A `match` that names every variant they have today would then stop covering them, so the compiler asks for a wildcard arm now, and the `match` keeps compiling when a variant arrives. Listing every current variant is not enough. Add `_`, or `Err(_)` where the enum is wrapped, and put there whatever should happen for a variant you did not name. An enum of your own with the same name is not extensible; the rule follows the first-party enum (`HttpResult` is a reserved name). A `match` in a suite case is not checked. For an ordinary enum, a missing arm is `bynk.types.non_exhaustive_match`.
summary: A `match` covers an extensible standard-library enum (`FetchError`, `Method`) or the built-in `HttpResult` without a wildcard; it may gain variants in a minor release.
